report_name: CRPxO Ransomware Group Hits Aviation and Healthcare Targets

threat_actors.name: CRPxO
threat_actors.description: A ransomware operator that follows the Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) model, employing a double extortion strategy. The group targets U.S. organizations in critical sectors like aviation and healthcare, exfiltrating sensitive data before deploying ransomware.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through data encryption and the threat of leaking stolen data.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Attachment
attack_patterns.description: A typical initial access vector for ransomware groups like CRPxO, using phishing emails with malicious attachments to gain a foothold in the victim's network.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: A typical initial access vector for ransomware groups like CRPxO, involving the exploitation of unpatched vulnerabilities in public-facing services such as VPNs or RDP.

attack_patterns.name: Archive via Utility
attack_patterns.description: Before exfiltration, the CRPxO group collects and compresses sensitive data from victim file servers and databases.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: The CRPxO group exfiltrates stolen data to cloud storage or actor-controlled servers, often using tools like rclone.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The CRPxO ransomware payload is executed across the victim's network to encrypt files, disrupting operations and holding the data for ransom.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: CRPxO operators likely delete volume shadow copies using tools like vssadmin.exe or wmic.exe to prevent easy restoration of encrypted files.

attack_patterns.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
attack_patterns.description: Ransomware like CRPxO may use registry run keys for persistence on compromised systems.

malware.name: CRPxO Ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware payload deployed by the CRPxO group to encrypt victim systems as part of their double extortion attacks.

tools.name: Cobalt Strike
tools.description: A post-exploitation framework typically used by the CRPxO group to maintain access and escalate privileges after gaining initial access.

tools.name: rclone
tools.description: A command-line program used by ransomware groups like CRPxO to exfiltrate large volumes of data to cloud storage providers.

identities.name: Qube Aviation Catering
identities.description: An aviation catering company in the U.S. targeted by the CRPxO ransomware group, which claimed to have exfiltrated 22.5 GB of data.

identities.name: ProSmile Family Dental Care
identities.description: A U.S. dental care provider targeted by the CRPxO ransomware group, which claimed to have exfiltrated 9.6 GB of data.

identities.name: American Home Healthcare
identities.description: A U.S. home healthcare provider linked to a data breach by the CRPxO ransomware group.

infrastructure.name: CRPxO Exfiltration Server
infrastructure.description: Cloud storage or actor-controlled servers used by the CRPxO group to store exfiltrated data from victims.

indicators.name: Ransomware-associated Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: Ransomware-associated Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 2b8a1c9d-5e6f-4a3b-8c1d-9e8f7a6b5c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects commands used to delete volume shadow copies, a common technique used by ransomware to inhibit system recovery.
references:
  - https://www.dexpose.io/crpxo-ransomware-group-targets-qube-aviation-catering/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-28
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_vssadmin:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  selection_wmic:
    Image|endswith: '\wmic.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'shadowcopy'
      - 'delete'
  condition: 1 of selection_*
